Link your phones without a login.

One administrator sets up Firebase once. People using the plant app do not need an account, email or password.

  1. Keep your Firebase project on Spark (no-cost). Do not attach a billing account or switch to Blaze. There is no paid server, AI service, file-storage service or Cloud Function in this design.
  2. In Firebase’s sidebar, open Security → Authentication → Sign-in method and enable Anonymous.
  3. Under Databases & Storage → Realtime Database, create the database in Locked mode.
  4. Open its Rules tab. Replace the rules with the tested rules below, then click Publish. These rules restrict each collection to its linked devices; they do not make the database public.
  5. The app developer adds the public Firebase web configuration, including the database URL, to the app. It contains no administrator password or private key.
  6. Open the updated app on your first phone. Tap Start shared collection, then Invite phone.
  7. On the other phone, tap Join with a code and paste the invitation. No Google sign-in is required.

After linking

Changes sync while the app is open and online. Offline changes remain saved locally and upload when the app can reconnect. The other phone receives them while open online. There are no background notifications or guaranteed closed-app syncing.

Keep using Save full backup occasionally. If a phone’s website data is cleared or its anonymous identity is lost, it needs a new invitation from the first phone. The project owner can manage access in Firebase.

On Spark, Realtime Database has free usage limits. If a limit is reached, cloud sync may pause; the app keeps local records. Do not enable billing as a workaround if you want the project to remain free.
